ports.functionality: Provides the response record back to the core, assembled from system response fields and the local sc_fail result; it exports err, ack and data to the core.
ports.evidence: concurrent assignments: core_rsp_o.err/ack/data <= expressions using sys_rsp_i and sc_fail

ports.name: core_rsp_o.ack
ports.functionality: Sends ack back to the core; it is driven by sys_rsp_i.ack ORed with sc_fail so either system ack or local SC failure asserts the core ack output.
ports.evidence: concurrent assignment: core_rsp_o.ack <= sys_rsp_i.ack or sc_fail

ports.name: core_rsp_o.err
ports.functionality: Forwards the system error status directly to the core response err field without modification.
ports.evidence: concurrent assignment: core_rsp_o.err <= sys_rsp_i.err

ports.name: core_rsp_o.data
ports.functionality: Delivers response data to the core built from sys_rsp_i.data upper 31..1 bits and LSB computed as sys_rsp_i.data(0) OR sc_fail, thus injecting SC result into response LSB.
ports.evidence: concurrent assignment: core_rsp_o.data <= sys_rsp_i.data(31 downto 1) & (sys_rsp_i.data(0) or sc_fail)

ports.name: sys_req_o
ports.functionality: Forwards core request fields to the system, copying core_req_i by default and adjusting the stb field when rvso indicates an AMO write to mask transmission using state(1).
ports.evidence: bus_request process: sys_req_o <= core_req_i and sys_req_o.stb conditional assignments

ports.name: sys_req_o.addr
ports.functionality: Carries the address forwarded from core_req_i.addr via the aggregate copy to the system request output.
ports.evidence: bus_request process: sys_req_o <= core_req_i assigns the whole record

ports.name: sys_req_o.data
ports.functionality: Forwards core request data unchanged into the system request record via the aggregate assignment from core_req_i.
ports.evidence: bus_request process: sys_req_o <= core_req_i assigns the whole record

ports.name: sys_req_o.ben
ports.functionality: Forwards the core byte-enable field into the system request via the aggregate record assignment.
ports.evidence: bus_request process: sys_req_o <= core_req_i assigns the whole record

ports.name: sys_req_o.stb
ports.functionality: Produces the system strobe by default from core_req_i.stb, but when rvso is set and core_req_i.rw='1' it masks the strobe with state(1). Thus it conditionally suppresses system transmission for certain AMO writes.
ports.evidence: bus_request process: conditional sys_req_o.stb assignments using rvso, core_req_i.rw and state(1)

ports.name: sys_req_o.rw
ports.functionality: Forwards the read/write indicator from the core request into sys_req_o.rw by the aggregate copy performed in the bus_request process.
ports.evidence: bus_request process: sys_req_o <= core_req_i assigns the whole record

ports.name: sys_req_o.src
ports.functionality: Forwards the request source identifier from core_req_i into sys_req_o.src through the aggregate copy.
ports.evidence: bus_request process: sys_req_o <= core_req_i assigns the whole record

ports.name: sys_req_o.priv
ports.functionality: Carries the privilege bit from the core request and forwards it unchanged to sys_req_o.priv via the aggregate assignment.
ports.evidence: bus_request process: sys_req_o <= core_req_i assigns the whole record

ports.name: sys_req_o.debug
ports.functionality: Forwards the debug flag from the core request to the system request via the aggregate copy.
ports.evidence: bus_request process: sys_req_o <= core_req_i assigns the whole record

ports.name: sys_req_o.amo
ports.functionality: Propagates the AMO flag from the core to the system request via the aggregate copy performed in bus_request.
ports.evidence: bus_request process: sys_req_o <= core_req_i assigns the whole record

ports.name: sys_req_o.amoop
ports.functionality: Forwards the AMO opcode bits from the core request to the system via the aggregate record assignment.
ports.evidence: bus_request process: sys_req_o <= core_req_i assigns the whole record

ports.name: sys_req_o.lock
ports.functionality: Forwards the lock bit from the core request into sys_req_o.lock by the aggregate copy.
ports.evidence: bus_request process: sys_req_o <= core_req_i assigns the whole record

ports.name: sys_req_o.fence
ports.functionality: Forwards the fence attribute from the core request unchanged into sys_req_o.fence through the aggregate assignment.
ports.evidence: bus_request process: sys_req_o <= core_req_i assigns the whole record

ports.name: sys_rsp_i
ports.functionality: Supplies the system response record fields (err, ack, data) that the entity uses to build core_rsp_o outputs; sys_rsp_i values feed core_rsp_o.err, ack and data computations.
ports.evidence: concurrent assignments use sys_rsp_i.err/ack/data to compute core_rsp_o.err/ack/data

ports.name: sys_rsp_i.ack
ports.functionality: Provides the system ack used directly to form core_rsp_o.ack (ORed with sc_fail); its assertion clears the FSM when observed in rvs_control.
ports.evidence: core_rsp_o.ack <= sys_rsp_i.ack or sc_fail; rvs_control when "11" checks sys_rsp_i.ack

ports.name: sys_rsp_i.err
ports.functionality: Carries the system error flag and is forwarded directly to core_rsp_o.err without modification.
ports.evidence: concurrent assignment: core_rsp_o.err <= sys_rsp_i.err

ports.name: sys_rsp_i.data
ports.functionality: Provides the 32-bit response data used to build core_rsp_o.data: bits 31..1 are passed through and bit0 is ORed with sc_fail to become the LSB returned to the core.
ports.evidence: core_rsp_o.data <= sys_rsp_i.data(31 downto 1) & (sys_rsp_i.data(0) or sc_fail)

signals.name: state
signals.functionality: Holds the current arbiter state across cycles; captured from state_nxt on clock and used as the case selector that drives FSM behaviour and guards internal register updates.
signals.evidence: state <= state_nxt (arbiter_sync rising_edge); used as 'case state is' in arbiter_fsm and in arbiter_sync 'if (state = S_BUSY_A)' checks

signals.name: state_nxt
signals.functionality: Combinational next-state computed in arbiter_fsm from state, locks, sel_q, request strobes and x_rsp_i.ack; its value is captured into state on clock.
signals.evidence: state_nxt defaulted and assigned in arbiter_fsm case branches using state, locked, sel_q, a_req/b_req and x_rsp_i.ack

signals.name: a_req
signals.functionality: Register that latches whether A has asserted stb; ORs incoming a_req_i.stb each cycle and is cleared when state indicates A is being served. Used by FSM to consider pending A requests.
signals.evidence: a_req <= '0' or a_req or a_req_i.stb in arbiter_sync; a_req tested in arbiter_fsm conditions

signals.name: b_req
signals.functionality: Register that latches whether B has asserted stb; ORs incoming b_req_i.stb each cycle and is cleared when state indicates B is being served. Used by FSM to consider pending B requests.
signals.evidence: b_req <= '0' or b_req or b_req_i.stb in arbiter_sync; b_req tested in arbiter_fsm conditions

signals.name: sel
signals.functionality: Combinational selection signal computed by the FSM that chooses between A and B for forwarding; it is captured into sel_q on clock and used to multiplex x_req_o fields and to route responses.
signals.evidence: sel <= '0'/'1' assignments in arbiter_fsm case branches; sel used in when-else assignments to x_req_o.* and response routing

signals.name: sel_q
signals.functionality: Holds the previous-cycle selection (captured from sel each clock) and biases arbitration order in the next arbitration decision.
signals.evidence: sel_q <= sel in arbiter_sync; sel_q used in arbiter_fsm 'if (sel_q = '1') or (not ROUND_ROBIN_EN)'

signals.name: stb
signals.functionality: Combinational strobe computed by the FSM from selection, lock and request strobes; drives x_req_o.stb to indicate the forwarded request to X.
signals.evidence: stb set in arbiter_fsm branches and assigned to x_req_o.stb

signals.name: locked
signals.functionality: Two-bit register holding captured lock state from locked_nxt each clock; used by the FSM to determine if the currently selected port holds a lock and whether to use incoming stb or wait for unlock/ack.
signals.evidence: locked <= locked_nxt in arbiter_sync; locked(0)/(1) tested in S_BUSY_A/S_BUSY_B branches to control stb and state_nxt

signals.name: locked_nxt
signals.functionality: Combinational next-lock value computed in arbiter_fsm (defaults from locked, or set to b_req_i.lock & a_req_i.lock) and captured into locked on clock.
signals.evidence: locked_nxt <= locked default; locked_nxt <= b_req_i.lock & a_req_i.lock in others branch of arbiter_fsm

signals.name: port_sel
signals.functionality: Combinationally computes which downstream port should receive the incoming request using address comparisons and X_EN fallback. Its bits gate port_req(i).stb and are captured into keeper.halt.
signals.evidence: port_sel(0..3) assigned by 'when' concurrent statements using req_i.addr and port_sel(2 downto 0) in port_sel(3) assignment

signals.name: port_req
signals.functionality: Combinationally assigned in the request process from req_i or a terminate constant; per-port entries carry request fields to the external a/b/c/x_req_o outputs.
signals.evidence: request process assigns port_req(i) <= req_terminate_c or <= req_i; port_req(i).stb <= port_sel(i) and req_i.stb; a_req_o <= port_req(0) etc.

signals.name: port_rsp
signals.functionality: Each index is driven from the corresponding *_rsp_i input via concurrent assignments and then read by the response process to build the aggregated int_rsp.
signals.evidence: port_rsp(0..3) <= a_rsp_i, b_rsp_i, c_rsp_i, x_rsp_i; response process reads port_rsp(i) to build tmp_v

signals.name: int_rsp
signals.functionality: Combinationally assigned from a temporary tmp_v in the response process which ORs data/ack/err from enabled port_rsp entries; then drives rsp_o fields and is read by keeper logic.
signals.evidence: response process builds tmp_v from port_rsp and assigns int_rsp <= tmp_v; bus_monitor tests int_rsp.ack

signals.name: int_rsp.ack
signals.functionality: Result of OR of port_rsp(i).ack fields; used to drive rsp_o.ack and to clear keeper.busy in bus_monitor on acknowledgement.
signals.evidence: tmp_v.ack := tmp_v.ack or port_rsp(i).ack; int_rsp <= tmp_v; bus_monitor uses (int_rsp.ack = '1') to clear keeper.busy

signals.name: int_rsp.err
signals.functionality: OR of port_rsp(i).err fields that is forwarded to rsp_o.err and indicates downstream error presence.
signals.evidence: tmp_v.err := tmp_v.err or port_rsp(i).err; int_rsp <= tmp_v; rsp_o.err <= int_rsp.err or keeper.err

signals.name: int_rsp.data
signals.functionality: Result of ORing port response data fields into tmp_v.data; presented on rsp_o.data to the upstream requester.
signals.evidence: tmp_v.data := tmp_v.data or port_rsp(i).data; int_rsp <= tmp_v; rsp_o.data <= int_rsp.data

signals.name: keeper
signals.functionality: Clocked record holding busy, lock, cnt, err and halt. It is reset by rstn_i and updated on rising_edge(clk_i) to implement timeout/lock monitoring and error signaling.
signals.evidence: keeper fields set in bus_monitor process's reset and rising_edge branches; keeper.err ORed into rsp_o.ack/err

signals.name: keeper.busy
signals.functionality: Set from req_i.stb when idle and cleared on int_rsp.ack, lock release, or timeout; gates counter updates and request capture behaviour.
signals.evidence: keeper.busy <= req_i.stb when keeper.busy = '0'; if (keeper.busy = '0') then ... else keeper.cnt <= unsigned(keeper.cnt)+1

signals.name: keeper.lock
signals.functionality: Captures req_i.lock when a request becomes busy and participates with req_i.lock to determine when to clear busy.
signals.evidence: keeper.lock <= req_i.lock when keeper.busy = '0'; condition ((keeper.lock = '1') and (req_i.lock = '0')) clears keeper.busy

signals.name: keeper.cnt
signals.functionality: Reset to zero when idle and incremented each clock while busy. Its top bit is tested to detect timeout and set keeper.err.
signals.evidence: keeper.cnt <= std_ulogic_vector(unsigned(keeper.cnt) + 1); check keeper.cnt(keeper.cnt'left) = '1' to set keeper.err

signals.name: keeper.err
signals.functionality: Set when the timeout counter saturates while not halted; cleared at each rising_edge start and ORed into rsp_o to report errors.
signals.evidence: keeper.err <= '0' at rising_edge start; set to '1' on timeout; used in rsp_o.ack/err assignments

signals.name: keeper.halt
signals.functionality: Captures the MSB of port_sel each clock and is used to inhibit timeout error generation while halt is asserted.
signals.evidence: keeper.halt <= port_sel(port_sel'left) in bus_monitor; condition (keeper.halt = '0') required to set keeper.err

signals.name: dev_req
signals.functionality: Holds a bus_req record for each device index; each element is assigned from main_req when its device is enabled or set to a terminate constant when disabled, and is exported to the corresponding dev_N_req_o output.
signals.evidence: bus_request processes assign dev_req(i) <= main_req and dev_xx_req_o <= dev_req(xx) concurrent assignments.

signals.name: dev_rsp
signals.functionality: Collects each device's response record via concurrent assignments from dev_N_rsp_i ports; this array is read by the bus_response process to compute the aggregated main_rsp.
signals.evidence: Concurrent assignments dev_rsp(i) <= dev_xx_rsp_i and bus_response process reads dev_rsp to build tmp_v then assigns main_rsp <= tmp_v.

signals.name: main_req
signals.functionality: Receives the device_req_o output from the instantiated bus register (neorv32_bus_reg_inst) and supplies the routed main request fields to the per-device dev_req(i) generators for address decoding and strobe gating.
signals.evidence: Port map connects device_req_o => main_req; bus_request processes use main_req and assign dev_req(i) <= main_req and dev_req(i).stb <= main_req.stb.

signals.name: main_req.addr
signals.functionality: Supplies the address bits of the internal main request used to select which device receives the strobe; compared against per-device base addresses to gate dev_req(i).stb.
signals.evidence: bus_request process compares main_req.addr(addr_hi_c downto addr_lo_c) = dev_base_list_c(i)(addr_hi_c downto addr_lo_c) to decide dev_req(i).stb.

signals.name: main_req.data
signals.functionality: Carries data payload from the internal main request to per-device dev_req elements; used as the source for dev_req(i).data when a device is enabled and the record is copied.
signals.evidence: bus_request process assigns dev_req(i) <= main_req; the whole record (including .data) is copied into dev_req elements.

signals.name: main_req.ben
signals.functionality: Carries byte-enable bits from the internal main request into per-device dev_req elements when copied, so the enabled device receives the same byte-enable information.
signals.evidence: dev_req(i) <= main_req in bus_request process copies .ben into dev_req elements.

signals.name: main_req.stb
signals.functionality: Provides the strobe bit that is conditionally forwarded into dev_req(i).stb by the routing logic when the address matches a device base; otherwise dev_req(i).stb is set to '0'.
signals.evidence: bus_request process sets dev_req(i).stb <= main_req.stb when address matches, else '0'.

signals.name: main_req.rw
signals.functionality: Carries the read/write bit from the internal main request into per-device dev_req elements when records are copied, indicating read or write to the selected device.
signals.evidence: dev_req(i) <= main_req in bus_request process copies .rw into dev_req elements.

signals.name: main_req.src
signals.functionality: Holds the source-id subfield of the internal main request which is copied into each dev_req(i).src when that dev_req element is assigned from main_req.
signals.evidence: dev_req(i) <= main_req copies .src as part of the record assignment in bus_request processes.

signals.name: main_req.priv
signals.functionality: Supplies the privilege flag from the internal main request into per-device dev_req elements when copied from main_req.
signals.evidence: dev_req(i) <= main_req in bus_request process copies .priv into dev_req.

signals.name: main_req.debug
signals.functionality: Carries the debug bit of the internal main request into dev_req elements when the main request record is forwarded to a device.
signals.evidence: bus_request process assigns dev_req(i) <= main_req, carrying .debug.

signals.name: main_req.amo
signals.functionality: Carries the AMO indicator from the internal main request into each dev_req element when forwarding the main request to a device.
signals.evidence: dev_req(i) <= main_req in bus_request process copies .amo.

signals.name: main_req.amoop
signals.functionality: Carries the AMO operation code from the internal main request into dev_req elements when records are copied for routing.
signals.evidence: dev_req(i) <= main_req copies .amoop as part of the whole-record assignment in bus_request.

signals.name: main_req.lock
signals.functionality: Holds the lock bit of the main request which is copied into dev_req elements when forwarding the main request to devices.
signals.evidence: dev_req(i) <= main_req in bus_request process copies .lock.

signals.name: main_req.fence
signals.functionality: Carries the fence bit of the main request into dev_req elements when requests are forwarded to devices as part of the whole-record copy.
signals.evidence: dev_req(i) <= main_req in bus_request process copies .fence.

signals.name: main_rsp
signals.functionality: Is assigned from the combined per-device dev_rsp values in the bus_response process (ORing fields) and is then provided to the instantiated bus register as device_rsp_i, supplying the register stage with the aggregated device responses.
signals.evidence: bus_response process ORs dev_rsp entries into tmp_v then assigns main_rsp <= tmp_v; port map connects device_rsp_i => main_rsp.

signals.name: main_rsp.ack
signals.functionality: Holds the aggregated ack bit computed by ORing dev_rsp(i).ack across enabled devices in the bus_response process; assigned into main_rsp.ack and then passed to the instantiated register input.
signals.evidence: bus_response process ORs dev_rsp(i).ack into tmp_v.ack then main_rsp <= tmp_v; port map device_rsp_i => main_rsp.

signals.name: main_rsp.err
signals.functionality: Holds the aggregated error bit produced by ORing dev_rsp(i).err across enabled devices in the bus_response process and is forwarded into the bus register input via the main_rsp signal.
signals.evidence: bus_response process ORs dev_rsp(i).err into tmp_v.err then assigns main_rsp <= tmp_v; instance mapped device_rsp_i => main_rsp.

signals.name: main_rsp.data
signals.functionality: Holds the aggregated data result computed by ORing dev_rsp(i).data across enabled devices in the bus_response process; assigned into main_rsp.data and provided to the bus register input.
signals.evidence: bus_response process does tmp_v.data := tmp_v.data or dev_rsp(i).data across loop then main_rsp <= tmp_v; instance maps device_rsp_i => main_rsp.

signals.name: arbiter
signals.function: holds AMO transaction state and data
signals.functionality: Register record that stores current AMO state, selected AMO command and read/write data. It is updated from arbiter_nxt on clk_i and read by combinational logic and ALU.
role: holds command and data across cycles
signals.evidence: arbiter <= arbiter_nxt on rising_edge(clk_i); arbiter fields read throughout arbiter_comb, amo_alu, and concurrent assignments

signals.name: arbiter.state
signals.functionality: Holds the finite-state-machine state for AMO handling. It is captured from arbiter_nxt on clock and selects transitions and output multiplexing in concurrent assignments and the comb process case.
signals.evidence: case arbiter.state is in arbiter_comb selects branches; concurrent assignments use arbiter.state in when conditions

signals.name: arbiter.cmd
signals.functionality: Holds the AMO opcode captured from arbiter_nxt.cmd; its low bits drive the ALU opcode case and its high bit steers signed/unsigned comparison behaviour in comparator logic.
signals.evidence: arbiter <= arbiter_nxt captures cmd; case arbiter.cmd(2 downto 0) in amo_alu; arbiter.cmd(3) used in cmp_opa/cmp_opb; arbiter.cmd(0) used in cmp_res condition

signals.name: arbiter.rdata
signals.functionality: Holds the read data captured into arbiter from arbiter_nxt.rdata; used as an operand for the ALU, comparator input, and as the response data returned to core when not idle.
signals.evidence: arbiter <= arbiter_nxt captures rdata; cmp_opa built from arbiter.rdata; alu_res cases use arbiter.rdata; core_rsp_o.data else branch uses arbiter.rdata

signals.name: arbiter.wdata
signals.functionality: Stores the write data captured into arbiter from arbiter_nxt.wdata; used as ALU operand and comparator input during AMO operations.
signals.evidence: arbiter <= arbiter_nxt captures wdata; arbiter.wdata used in amo_alu cases and cmp_opb expression

signals.name: arbiter_nxt
signals.functionality: Combinational record that starts as a copy of arbiter and is updated by the comb FSM logic to propose next state, command and data; its value is captured into arbiter on the clock.
signals.evidence: arbiter_nxt <= arbiter at process start; arbiter <= arbiter_nxt on rising_edge(clk_i)

signals.name: arbiter_nxt.state
signals.functionality: Combinational next-state field updated by arbiter_comb branches according to core_req_i and sys_rsp_i; it is later captured into arbiter.state on clk_i.
signals.evidence: arbiter_nxt <= arbiter default; branches in arbiter_comb assign arbiter_nxt.state; arbiter <= arbiter_nxt captures it on clk

signals.name: arbiter_nxt.cmd
signals.functionality: Combinational field set from core_req_i.amoop when accepting an AMO request in S_IDLE; later captured into arbiter.cmd on the clock.
signals.evidence: arbiter_nxt.cmd <= core_req_i.amoop in S_IDLE; default arbiter_nxt <= arbiter

signals.name: arbiter_nxt.rdata
signals.functionality: Combinational field that is assigned from sys_rsp_i.data in the read-wait state and otherwise defaults to current arbiter.rdata; captured into arbiter.rdata on clock.
signals.evidence: in S_READ_WAIT arbiter_nxt.rdata <= sys_rsp_i.data; default arbiter_nxt <= arbiter

signals.name: arbiter_nxt.wdata
signals.functionality: Combinational field loaded from core_req_i.data when an AMO is accepted and otherwise defaults from arbiter; captured into arbiter.wdata on clock.
signals.evidence: arbiter_nxt.wdata <= core_req_i.data in S_IDLE; default arbiter_nxt <= arbiter

signals.name: alu_res
signals.functionality: Synchronous register that holds the computed AMO/ALU result each clock. It captures arithmetic/bitwise results from arbiter.rdata/wdata or comparator result and is used as write data during AMO write phases.
role: provides write data to sys_req_o when writing
signals.evidence: amo_alu process assigns alu_res from arbiter.rdata/wdata/cmp_res at rising_edge(clk_i); sys_req_o.data uses alu_res when arbiter.state = S_WRITE

signals.name: cmp_opa
signals.functionality: Combinational 33-bit operand built by sign/zero extension of arbiter.rdata using arbiter.cmd(3) as sign control; used in the signed comparison and in selecting comparator result.
signals.evidence: cmp_opa <= (arbiter.rdata(arbiter.rdata'left) and arbiter.cmd(3)) & arbiter.rdata; cmp_opa used by signed(cmp_opa)

signals.name: cmp_opb
signals.functionality: Combinational 33-bit operand built by sign/zero extension of arbiter.wdata using arbiter.cmd(3) as sign control; used in the signed comparison and comparator selection.
signals.evidence: cmp_opb <= (arbiter.wdata(arbiter.wdata'left) and arbiter.cmd(3)) & arbiter.wdata; cmp_opb used by signed(cmp_opb)

signals.name: cmp_less
signals.functionality: Combinational single-bit result of signed(cmp_opa) < signed(cmp_opb). It participates in selecting cmp_res and thus affects ALU fallback behavior.
signals.evidence: cmp_less <= '1' when (signed(cmp_opa) < signed(cmp_opb)) else '0'; cmp_less used in cmp_res selection

signals.name: cmp_res
signals.functionality: Combinational 32-bit result selected from cmp_opa(31 downto 0) or cmp_opb(31 downto 0) based on (cmp_less xor arbiter.cmd(0)). It is the fallback ALU result for operations not covered by explicit opcodes.
signals.evidence: cmp_res <= cmp_opa(31 downto 0) when ((cmp_less xor arbiter.cmd(0)) = '1') else cmp_opb(31 downto 0); alu_res <= cmp_res in amo_alu when others

signals.name: state
signals.functionality: Holds the control FSM state across clock edges; it is reset to 0, used as the case selector to decide transitions, and bit1 gates sys_req_o.stb and contributes to sc_fail logic.
signals.evidence: rvs_control process: reset assigns state; case state is selects branches; bus_request and sc_result read state(1)

signals.name: rvso
signals.functionality: Combinational signal indicating a specific AMO (amo=1 and amoop[3:2]="10"); it gates state transitions in rvs_control and conditions sys_req_o.stb behaviour and sc_fail computation.
signals.evidence: rvso <= '1' when (core_req_i.amo = '1') and (core_req_i.amoop(3 downto 2) = "10") else '0'; rvso used in rvs_control, bus_request, sc_result

signals.name: sc_fail
signals.functionality: Registers the computed SC-failure condition at clock edge; it is reset to '0' and on rising edge captures rvso AND core_req_i.stb AND core_req_i.rw AND (not state(1)), then contributes to core_rsp_o.ack and core_rsp_o.data LSB.
signals.evidence: sc_result process: reset sets sc_fail; rising_edge captures rvso and core_req_i.stb,rw and state(1); core_rsp_o.ack/data use sc_fail
